question: The characteristic color of Marine Algae depends on the pigments located in the plastids. Which pigment leads to 'Green' colour of the algae?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chlorophyll**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Chlorophyll:**

 
 
• This is the primary pigment responsible for photosynthesis in plants and algae.
 
• It's a green pigment that absorbs light energy from the sun, particularly in the blue and red regions of the spectrum.
 
• This absorbed energy is then used to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose (sugar) through a complex series of chemical reactions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Carotene:**

 
 
• **​** This is a yellow-orange pigment found in plants, fruits, and vegetables.
 
• It belongs to a group of pigments called carotenoids.
 
• While it doesn't directly participate in photosynthesis, it plays a crucial role as an accessory pigment.
 
• Carotene absorbs light energy and transfers it to chlorophyll, enhancing the efficiency of photosynthesis.
 
 
 
• **Zeaxanthin: **
 
 
• **​**Another carotenoid pigment, zeaxanthin is responsible for the yellow-orange color of many fruits and vegetables, such as corn and peppers.
 
• It plays a vital role in protecting the eye from harmful blue light and oxidative damage.
 
• Zeaxanthin is also a powerful antioxidant, helping to protect cells from damage caused by free radicals.
 
 
 
• **Phycocyanin:**
 
 
• This is a blue-green pigment found in cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) and some red algae.
 
• It belongs to a group of pigments called phycobiliproteins.
 
• Phycocyanin absorbs light energy in the orange and red regions of the spectrum and transfers it to chlorophyll, enabling photosynthesis in these organisms.
